pages.text: "The boat's coming! I'll board first!" Mina ran to the landing. Mom, carrying the packed things, called them back. "You need to carry your things, too."
"Let's buy green fruit first at the market!" Mina waved empty hands. Mom opened one. "Where will you put the fruit?"
Mina curved both arms. The space inside was empty. There was nowhere for lots of fruit. "Oh, that won't work!"
The boatman pulled alongside. "We'll leave when the sun reaches above that tree." It was still below. Mom sat facing Mina on the dirt.
Mom set down a basket, then a water bottle, then a towel. "These three will help us at the market." Mina pointed to each. "Basket, Water Bottle, Towel—Three!"
Mina held the basket. One! The bottle's strap went over a shoulder. Two! The towel wrapped around the neck, ends tucked snugly. Three!
Rowing, the boatman smiled. "Well packed!" Mina held Mom's hand and sat inside the boat. "Basket, Water Bottle, Towel—Three!"
In the middle of the river, Mina drank from the bottle. Mom said, "There's nowhere to buy water out here." Mina closed the cap tightly.
On the next market morning, Mina packed the basket, bottle, and towel one by one. "I brought everything this time!"
That evening, the boat reached the landing. Mom hugged Mina. Fruit filled Mina's basket. "I'll give Sonu one, too."
